entries.title: Gemini Decisions API: Fast, calibrated multimodal decisions
entries.summary: Meet the Gemini Decisions API, powered by our state-of-the-art model Gemini Decision for fast, calibrated multimodal decisions.
entries.content:
Today, we’re introducing the Gemini Decisions API, a new endpoint for fast, closed-set decisions powered by our new Gemini Decision 1 model (gemini-decision-1), available through the Gemini API in Google AI Studio.

The Decisions API gives you purpose-built primitives for bounded choices like tool selection, policy checks, model routing, and context grading. You can pass one multimodal input across text, images, audio, video, and PDFs (up to 256K tokens) along with up to 1,000 independent questions. Rather than generating answer text token by token, Gemini Decision 1 scores your candidate options in a single forward pass, returning probabilities and confidence scores in 150-250 ms end-to-end latency at $0.10 per 1M input tokens with zero output tokens billed.

Strong performance and calibration

On benchmarks spanning agent routing, reasoning, ranking, and multimodal understanding, Gemini Decision 1 leads across the suite, with the lowest calibration error.

Gemini Decision 1 scores options without token-by-token decoding, keeping median latency 50-100 ms of model compute (150-250 ms end-to-end), across multimodal inputs and contexts up to 16K tokens, remaining nearly flat from 1 to 100 questions per request. With zero output tokens billed, Gemini Decision 1 with the Decisions API is nearly 5x cheaper across the shared benchmark suite than Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite with the Interactions API.

Native multimodal evaluation across three decision types in one pass

Built on Gemini’s native multimodal architecture, Gemini Decision 1 can process text, images, audio, video, and PDFs directly in a single forward pass. You can combine modalities in one shared input, such as pairing a call recording with account metadata or a scanned PDF claim with damage photos, and tune resolution on image and video inputs to control visual detail and token cost.

You can evaluate multiple questions against that shared input in a single request, mixing yes/no checks, multiple choice, and rubric scores. Every answer includes a confidence score (from 0 to 1) so your code can route ambiguous cases to a fallback or human reviewer:

  • noul (Yes/No): Estimates the probability that a yes/no condition holds, with optional true and false description criteria.
  • choice (Multiple Choice): Selects from 2 to 255 choices, returning the winner and normalized probabilities for every candidate.
  • score (Ordered Rubric): Grades inputs across an ordered rubric (starting at 0), returning a continuous weighted score and per-level probabilities.

The 

input
field uses the same 
Content
block format as the Interactions API. Here is how to check a photo of a breakroom counter, together with a text note, against all three question types in one request:
from google import genai

client = genai.Client(http_options={"api_version": "v1beta"})

result = client.decisions.create(
    model="gemini-decision-1",
    input=[{
            "type": "image",
            "uri": "https://storage.googleapis.com/generativeai-downloads/images/spill.jpg",
            "mime_type": "image/jpeg",
        },
        {
            "type": "text",
            "text": "Breakroom counter check before the 9 AM client meeting.",
        },
    ],
    questions={
        "has_spill": {
            "type": "noul",
            "instructions": "Is there an uncleaned liquid spill on the counter?",
        },
        "next_action": {
            "type": "choice",
            "instructions": "Which cleanup action fits the scene?",
            "criteria": {
                "wipe_with_cloth": "Small counter spill with a cloth or towel already nearby.",
                "dispatch_janitorial": "Large floor hazard, broken glass, or active leak.",
                "ready_for_meeting": "Counter is clean and ready.",
            },
        },
        "severity": {
            "type": "score",
            "instructions": "Rate the severity of the counter mess.",
            "criteria": [
                "Clean and ready.",
                "Minor localized spill.",
                "Major spill or safety hazard.",
            ],
        },
    },
)

How teams are building with the Decisions API

Teams across Google are already using the Decisions API as a low-latency control plane, shipping features simply by defining options rather than training custom classifiers or waiting on generative calls:

  • Dynamic model routing in Gemini Notebook: Gemini Notebook uses the Decisions API as a real-time router to instantly direct incoming queries to the optimal model tier and thinking level for each request. The Decisions API classifies intent in milliseconds to serve everyday queries with up to 40% lower latency while reserving deep reasoning models for complex tasks.
  • Rapid design iteration in Stitch: The new rapid canvas experiment in Stitch uses the Decisions API to generate playable wireframes of a product flow in seconds and to apply edits made by voice or tap almost instantly. When the flow feels right, one click hands the screens off to the full Stitch experience for deeper design polish.
  • Emoji selection in CC: CC from Google Labs uses the Decisions API to pick the right emoji reaction from a palette of more than 200 options in a fraction of a second, so reactions appear instantly without adding latency.
  • Safety layer for MCP tools in Search: Google Search uses the Decision API to detect adversarial behavior and content against adversarial evals with high efficacy within the latency envelope.

Stitch Rapid uses the Decisions API to design an entire product flow in seconds (1x speed).

Start building today

Gemini Decision 1 is priced at $0.10 per 1M input tokens and $0 for output tokens, with an API no-cost tier you can use in Google AI Studio for prototyping. Your shared 

input
is billed once per request no matter how many questions you evaluate (each question adds only its own instruction and criteria tokens). There are no output-token charges, variable thinking-token bills, or separate audio transcription and OCR costs.

You can start building today by grabbing an API key in Google AI Studio, trying our Doorstep Parcels, Speed Sketch, and Find the Zoo Keeper demo apps, and following the Python, JavaScript, and REST guides in the Decisions API documentation.

Ecosystem integrations are rolling out across OpenRouter, LangChain, Vercel, LiteLLM, Pydantic AI, Pipecat, LiveKit, and OpenCode alongside the 

google-genai
SDKs, with support coming soon to Gemini in Google Cloud.

entries.title: Built on Googlebook: Play Henry Cavill’s video game to support Movember
entries.summary: The video shows Henry Cavill making his video game on Googlebook.
entries.content:
Henry Cavill teamed up with Google to build “Mustache Protocol,” a 16-bit video game, on his Googlebook. Over the past few weeks, we’ve watched Henry’s creative process unfold. In the first episode of our behind-the-scenes series, he designed a handlebar-mustachioed hero using Magic Pointer and Quick Access. In the second episode, he used Rambler to create superpowers and health boosts. Today, we’re sharing the final episode — and the game is officially ready for you to play.

Watch the episode

In the third episode of the series, Henry puts the finishing touches on his game. Every great game needs a theme song, and the finale shows how with a little help from Googlebook, Henry brought the game’s audio together. Let’s dive in:

  • Continue On: Henry previewed a smooth, ’70s-style track on his Android phone, then used Continue On to move the music to his Googlebook desktop without interrupting his flow.
  • Rambler and BandLab: After Henry plugged in a drum pad to add custom musical beats using BandLab and recorded sultry baritone vocals, Rambler turned his voice commands into clean prompts to drop the track and sound effects into the game.
  • Antigravity: Using Antigravity, the next-gen agentic platform built into Googlebook, Henry stitched together the final visuals, level layouts, and interactive elements — the last steps in taking the game from an idea to a live, playable build.

Play “Mustache Protocol” and support Movember

“Mustache Protocol” is ready for you to play. The retro-style game sends players on an epic quest across three levels to stop a rogue CGI agent from erasing every mustache on the planet. It is, as Henry told us, "super serious."

You can play directly in your web browser or on your desktop or mobile device using simple arcade controls to move, jump, and swing your mustache-comb sword. To make the game uniquely his, Henry packed each level with hilarious power-ups and Easter eggs. See if you can spot all of them.

In honor of Movember, your gameplay supports men’s health. From November 11 to 30, for every game played, Google will donate $11 to Movember, up to $500,000. Every play helps drive awareness and funding for men’s mental health, suicide prevention, prostate cancer, and testicular cancer.

So fire up your browser and help us save the world’s mustaches. Head to googlebook.com/henry to play “Mustache Protocol,” watch all three episodes, and join the movement.

entries.title: Talk it through with Gemini, now on Apple CarPlay
entries.summary: an MP4 video of Gemini in Apple CarPlay
entries.content:
For millions of people, the daily commute averages about an hour behind the wheel. While voice assistants have long been great for quick tasks like playing a playlist or getting directions home, all that quiet time on the road is also an opportunity to catch up, prepare for what’s ahead, or simply think out loud.

Following our rollout on Android Auto and cars with Google built-in, today we’re bringing the Gemini app directly to Apple CarPlay. Now, iOS users can have natural, free-flowing conversations with Gemini Live right from their car’s display — hands-free, so you can get more done while keeping your hands on the wheel and your eyes on the road.

Pick up where you left off — or start a fresh conversation

We designed Gemini on CarPlay to work like a conversational driving companion that minimizes distraction. When you tap the Gemini app icon on your CarPlay screen or side rail, you can easily pick up where you left off with a recent chat or start a fresh conversation.

You can talk back and forth with Gemini at your own pace — interrupting to add a detail, changing the subject, or pausing when you need to focus on an exit.

Make the most of your drive

Whether you’re commuting or setting out on a road trip, Gemini on CarPlay helps you be more productive during your ride. Here are a few ways to make the most of your drive:

  • Get ready for the day ahead: Use your morning commute to see what's coming up and walk into your first meeting prepared. Ask Gemini what's on your calendar, when you need to leave for your next appointment, or talk through what you want to say before you arrive.
    • Try saying: "What does my day look like?" or "Help me prep for my 10am with the design team."
  • Talk through your inbox: Because Gemini connects with your Google Workspace apps like Gmail and Google Calendar, you can ask for your daily brief 1 , catch up on unread emails, get quick summaries of long email threads, and talk through a quick reply using just your voice.
    • Try saying: “Give me my daily brief for today,” or “Catch me up on my unread emails and summarize Sarah’s Q4 budget thread.”
  • Explore local spots and landmarks: Ask Gemini for recommendations in the area you’re heading to, from a quick place to grab lunch to the backstory on a local landmark.
    • Try saying: “What’s a quick lunch spot in downtown Austin that’s easy to get in and out of?”
  • Brainstorm, rehearse, and learn out loud: A quiet car cabin is one of the best places to think out loud. Use Gemini Live as a sounding board to practice an upcoming presentation, prepare for a tough conversation, or break down a complex topic you’ve been curious about.
    • Try saying: “Let’s roleplay my Q4 pitch — act as a skeptical VP and challenge my strategy,” or “Break down how solid-state EV batteries work in simple terms.”

And because your CarPlay conversations sync automatically with the Gemini app on your iPhone, every summary, note, and brainstorm is waiting in your chat history the moment you park.

Get started today

Gemini on Apple CarPlay is rolling out globally starting today to all Gemini users on iOS across every supported Gemini Live language.

To get started, make sure you’ve updated to the latest version of the Gemini app on your iPhone, enabled microphone permissions, and used Gemini Live on your phone at least once. The next time you connect your phone to your car, tap the Gemini icon on your CarPlay display, then start a new conversation or pick up a recent one.

entries.title: Google’s ongoing commitment to the veteran community
entries.summary: Google logo with a box of medals in front of it
entries.content:
As co-leads of the Google Veterans Network (VetNet) Employee Resource Group, we see daily how veterans’ skills translate into high-impact workforce leadership. Through deep collaborations with global non-profits, industry partners, and our own product teams, Google is continuing to invest in career pathways and grassroots support to help veterans and military spouses successfully transition and thrive at every stage of their civilian lives.

Expanding skills and career pathways

A central part of our efforts is providing veterans with career resources and trainings in the latest tech skills. Here’s what we’re doing:

  • Google Launchpad for Veterans: Now in its third year, this program helps active-duty personnel, transitioning service members, and veterans build practical cloud and generative AI skills, preparing them for credentials like the Generative AI Leader certification. Certifications — available at no cost through this program — are known to help open up career opportunities. In fact, 92% of Google Skills learners say Google Cloud credentials (certifications, skill badges) help them get in-demand jobs faster. 1
  • Veterans Career Week: Hosted alongside Grow with Google, our flagship initiative expanded internationally this year programming across the U.S., Europe, and Asia-Pacific, reaching over 6,000 participants. At our hands-on Grow with Google workshops, veterans and military families used tools like Career Dreamer, which translates their military experience into civilian resumes. They also received no-cost scholarships for digital and AI training, including the Google AI Professional Certificate. Today, one in ten Google Career Certificate graduates comes from the military community.
  • National Veterans Small Business Week: Grow with Google teamed up with American Corporate Partners (ACP) and Blue Star Families to deliver hands-on AI training during our third annual National Veterans Small Business Week livestream. Attendees learned practical AI skills and gained insights from a veteran-owned small business.
  • Skilled Trades Initiative: Google.org is supporting Hiring Our Heroes, Home Builders Institute, and Student Veterans of America to help 25,000 veterans and military family members build long-term careers in skilled trades. This builds upon prior funding to support student veterans nationwide with broad career readiness programming, including access to Google Career Certificates and Google AI Professional Certificate.
  • Public Sector Enablement: Working alongside partners like Carahsoft, Google Cloud has trained more than 40,000 public sector personnel, including active duty service members and reservists, equipping our military with the hands-on expertise to safely architect what’s next.

Investing in community organizations

This year’s Google Veteran Impact Awards delivered $500,000 in new funding across four high-impact organizations. Nominated by VetNet Googlers with deep personal ties to their work, these nonprofits represent the groups our veteran community trusts, champions, and volunteers for:

Spotlighting veterans through our products

Across Google's products and platforms, we are celebrating and connecting the military community:

  • Google Beam and USO: In partnership with the USO, we’re expanding HP Dimension with Google Beam to 20 locations globally. Powered by AI and 3D technology, Beam provides true-to-life video communication that lets deployed service members and their families feel like they are stepping into the same space. Watch our docuseries connecting four soldiers in Poland with their families in Texas; goo.gle/uso-beam
  • Google Doodle: Our annual Veterans Day Doodle recognizes service, dedication, and courage with the achievement medals representing the six branches of service. These merit-based awards, which honor exceptional teamwork or technical achievements, often represent a junior officer’s, warrant officer’s, or enlisted service member's first individual award for superior performance of their duties and are an important point of pride in veteran life.

Camaraderie and purpose don’t end when service members hang up their uniforms. For the thousands of military families transitioning to civilian life each year, that shared sense of mission endures — and at Google, we recognize that the resilience, adaptability, and teamwork forged in service are invaluable assets to our teams.

To our veterans, service members, and military families: thank you for your service and leadership.

entries.title: Google Cloud leaders share what to expect in cybersecurity for 2027.
entries.summary: In our Security 2027 analysis, leaders from across Google, Google Cloud, and Mandiant break down the critical trends shaping the next era of defense.
entries.content:
As enterprise software shifts from static applications to autonomous agents managing core operations, cybersecurity is facing a fundamental transformation. In our Security 2027 analysis, leaders from across Google, Google Cloud, and Mandiant break down the critical trends shaping the next era of defense.

Key priorities for 2027 include :

  • Protecting decision integrity: Ensuring every consequential autonomous action is secure and 100% explainable
  • Moving "Beyond Zero": Never blindly trusting any AI tool, and having visibility into what they can access and what they are doing
  • Winning with ground truth: Using multi-model AI ensembles to correlate internal context and remediate risks at machine speed before attackers can piece them together

Watch the Security 2027 overview video below, and read the full executive perspective on the Google Cloud Blog.

entries.title: Get certified as a Google Cloud Professional Agentic Architect.
entries.summary: Today we announced Google Cloud's new Professional Agentic Architect certification.
entries.content:
Today we announced Google Cloud's new Professional Agentic Architect certification: an industry-recognized certification that proves you can deploy secure, enterprise-grade agents that automate multi-step and multi-app workflows.

This hybrid certification has two parts: a proctored multiple-choice exam assessing foundational knowledge in agentic architecture, and Google Skills labs to evaluate real-world, hands-on practical experience.

Over the past four months, Google Cloud has trained thousands of Google Cloud forward deployed engineers and Google Cloud partners on this advanced curriculum. This certification is now available for technical professionals like developers, cloud architects, and engineers who architect, build, and deploy agents on Google Cloud.

Our research shows more than 80% of Google Cloud certified individuals say the credential opens doors to new career opportunities and accelerates their path to promotion. Furthermore, 82% of individuals say certifications from Google Cloud help them earn higher salaries 1 .

Start your preparation at no cost today. Sign up for Gemini Agent Ready to claim 35 free monthly learning credits and gain access to our hands-on labs and agentic courses.

Learn more on our Google Cloud blog.

entries.title: Try Tabletop: Customizable, collaborative spaces for groups to plan, play and do more together.
entries.summary: Tabletop is a new Google Labs experiment for group collaboration. Build interactive itineraries, polls, and brackets with your team. Join the waitlist.
entries.content:
Whether you’re planning a family trip, running a rec league or hosting a potluck, coordinating as a group is easier when everyone can pitch in, build and decide together in one place.

Today, we’re introducing Tabletop, a new Google Labs experiment built for real-time collaboration.

Just add in your links, files, and ideas, then prompt @tabletop — or pick a starter template — to generate custom interactive trip itineraries, dinner polls, expense splitters, and tournament brackets. Once your space is ready, drop the invite link in your group chat to let everyone jump in and use it at the same time, like in a Google Doc.

Tabletop is rolling out in the U.S. (18+) via waitlist. Pull up a chair and sign up at labs.google/tabletop.

entries.title: Experience the art and legacy of Dr. Esther Mahlangu
entries.summary: A portrait of Dr Nontobeko Ntombela, Senior Lecturer, Department of Curatorial, Public and Visual Cultures, Wits School of Arts, University of the Witwatersrand
entries.content:
Today we’re sharing the first online retrospective of artist Dr. Esther Mahlangu on Google Arts & Culture, honoring her pioneering spirit on her 91st birthday. More than 45 stories and a rich archive covering her art, life, and legacy are now accessible to a global audience.

For many years, I have worked closely with Esther and her family. It’s a relationship built on years of research and a deep admiration for her as both an artist and a person. It was out of this long-standing connection that the vision for “‘Then I Knew I Was Good at Painting’: Esther Mahlangu, a Retrospective,” was born.

My goal has always been to present a comprehensive exploration of her life and work, contributing to my long-standing research on South African women artists who have made an impact on the arts since the early 20th century.

Through my research, I gathered a rich collection of her work, including large-scale murals, intimate pieces, and rare archival materials. But the archives didn’t include anything from her life before 1980, so crucial pieces of her history were missing. This void challenged us to find new ways to tell her full story.

A collaboration session with Esther Mahlangu, Nontobeko Ntombela, and the Google team.

In collaboration with Google Arts & Culture, we used AI to visually recreate Esther’s undocumented memories. The process brought us closer to her work and prompted further recollections from Esther herself.

This project brought our curatorial and archival work together with the technical expertise of Google DeepMind and Google Arts & Culture Lab, alongside research and design studio Domestic Data Streamers’ synthetic memories initiative. Through a series of workshops and interviews, we were able to document a missing period of Mam' Esther's history, from when she started painting at age 10 until her first documented works in 1980. These stories — such as the moment she discovered her talent for painting as a 10-year-old using feathers instead of a brush — became the source material for our work. Following the methodology from the synthetic memories initiative and using archival material, the team generated still images based on Esther’s memories. They then used Veo to turn the images into videos that brought Esther's early days to life.

The stories also contribute to the online archive of Esther’s life on Google Arts & Culture. More than 45 exhibitions, curated in collaboration with Art of Contemporary Africa, Iziko Museums of South Africa, the British Museum, the Jean Pigozzi Collection, the National Museum of Women in the Arts, and Serpentine, tell the story of how she came to be known in the world, through her artwork, archives, Street View, and more.

This project demonstrates a new way to approach the preservation of cultural heritage, with technology that’s guided at every step by a respect for personal memory and historical accuracy.

It is my hope that this retrospective cements Esther’s place as a pivotal voice in global contemporary art, invites audiences to reimagine the possibilities of her archive, and ensures her story and her artistic vision can inspire generations to come.

Explore the exhibition at goo.gle/esther-mahlangu.

entries.title: Gemini Intelligence: New features, on more devices
entries.summary: A man speaks into a phone. Text on the screen reads 'Gemini Intelligence'
entries.content:
Gemini Intelligence 1 brings the best of Gemini to Android devices, helping your devices work harder for you. Earlier this year, we announced Gemini Intelligence, and this summer devices started rolling out — from the Pixel 11 to the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra, Z Fold8, Z Flip8 and S26 series. 2 Today, we’re introducing new features built for Gemini Intelligence, and expanding capabilities to more of Android’s most advanced devices. 3 Here’s a look at what’s new.

Gemini Intelligence on more devices, including motorola signature 27 and Pixel 10

Gemini Intelligence is coming to even more devices. Motorola is introducing its first Gemini Intelligence device, motorola signature 27, which is available for pre-order in the U.S. on November 19. And with today’s Pixel Drop, Pixel 10, Pixel 10 Pro XL, and Pixel 10 Pro Fold get the latest features for Gemini Intelligence.

Alongside this expansion, we’re bringing some of our favorite capabilities to more devices and regions, helping handle the busywork so you can focus on what matters. Rambler 4 — which turns spoken thoughts into clean, organized text in real-time — is now available on Pixel 10, Pixel 10 Pro, Pixel 10, Pro XL and Pixel 10 Pro Fold, as well as the new motorola signature 27. And task automation 5 — which lets you ask Gemini to handle logistics like ordering food, hailing rides, or booking reservations across your favorite apps — is expanding to the UK, India, and Japan.

Build custom widgets with a prompt

Create My Widget 6 , which is rolling out over the next few weeks, lets you design a personalized widget with a simple description in your own words — no coding required. Whether you want a dashboard for your upcoming trip, a monthly spending tracker, or a race day countdown, Create My Widget can pull in information from Gmail, Calendar, and Search to create a custom widget just for you, giving you the information you want at a glance on your homescreen.

Get personalized tech support with Device Assistance

Device Assistance 7 helps you control, change, or fix your device by just asking your phone for help. Ask Gemini to clear up space on your device, check which apps can access your location, or mute distractions while making sure important calls still come through. Gemini deeply understands your device so it can act as your personal device expert.

Experience proactive help across a range of screens

Gemini Intelligence is designed to support you across whatever screen you’re using. Last month we launched Googlebook, the first laptop designed for Gemini Intelligence.

And if you have a Pixel phone with Gemini Intelligence, it will soon bring proactive suggestions to Android Auto — connecting the dots across your apps to surface helpful, personalized suggestions 8 when you need them. For example, if your friend texts you to ask where you are meeting for a pilates class, Gemini Intelligence on Android Auto can find your confirmation email and instantly suggest sending the address with a single tap.

Plus, in the next few weeks, Create My Widget is coming to Pixel Watch. You’ll be able to design widgets that keep the details that matter to you right on your wrist.

entries.title: Pixel 10 with Gemini Intelligence, custom widgets, and more in our November Pixel Drop
entries.summary: Pixel Drop text with the Google G logo and irridescent squares
entries.content:
Our November Pixel Drop is here, with new and expanded features making your Pixel devices more personalized, intuitive, and handy. See how we’re bringing smarter automation, next-level personalization, and upgraded connectivity to your favorite devices. Updates start rolling out today and will continue over the next several weeks.

Use Pixel 10 with Gemini Intelligence

Gemini Intelligence is now available on Pixel 10 devices, bringing new capabilities like Rambler, personalized suggestions, and taking care of multi-step tasks — like placing your morning coffee order.

Polish your messages with Rambler on Pixel 10: Voice typing just got a major upgrade. Rambler can automatically remove filler words like “um,” and format your thoughts into clear, polished text. Just speak naturally, review, and send.

Complete multi-step tasks with Gemini: Whether you’re getting groceries, booking a ride, ordering takeout, or trying to find a reservation at your favorite restaurant, let Gemini handle the logistics so you can focus on other tasks. Now available in Japan, UK, and India.

Receive proactive suggestions: From sharing your ETA with a tap when someone asks when you’ll arrive, to helping you find the perfect dinner spot, your Pixel anticipates what you need with timely information and suggested actions, so you can accomplish your daily tasks faster. 1 Also, coming soon to Pixel Watch 4.

Create more personalized widgets: Ever find yourself wanting a widget that doesn’t seem to exist? Create personalized widgets, like a tracker to follow your monthly spending, a game day widget with your team colors, or a getaway countdown that automatically pulls in flight and reservation details. Your home screen can be as personalized as you want it to be. Also, coming soon to Pixel Watch 4 and Pixel Watch 5. 2

Catch up on long conversations: Your Pixel can now provide summaries of your longer conversations, so you can see what’s important right away. Now available in German, French, Spanish, Italian, Hindi, and Traditional Chinese. Coming to Pixel Watches soon. 3

Call Screen got an upgrade on Pixel 11 series

Whenever you see a call from an unknown number and choose to screen it, Gemini will ask unknown callers why they're reaching out in a much more conversational manner handling the exchange until you decide to jump in or end the call. With a live transcript displayed right on your screen, you can easily follow along and decide exactly when to pick up. Also, coming to Pixel Watch 4 and Pixel Watch 5 soon. 4

Personalize your Pixel with new custom icon styles

Following the launch of Custom Icons earlier this year, we’re adding more styles to give you even more ways to personalize your home screen Pixel. Pick from distinct styles that apply across all your app icons on the home screen. 5

New updates coming to Pixel search

Now available on Pixel 6 and newer devices, Pixel search helps you find what you need across your phone – from vacation photos and recent emails to messages, calendar events, and device settings. 6

Stay in the moment with Google Messages and HiLight

HiLight now supports Google Messages. When your phone is face down, HiLight will glow if you receive a message from one of your favorite contacts — letting you stay present without missing important messages or calls. 7

Keep tabs on your belongings with Pixel Tag

Pixel Tag offers peace of mind so you always know where your most important things are — and it’s available November 11. It’s slim enough to fit in your wallet and durable enough to attach to your belongings, with a battery that lasts over a year. The Find Hub network of more than 1 billion Android devices helps you locate your belongings even if they are miles away and UWB enables visual direction and distance guidance to find it nearby. 8 Pixel Tag is available starting November 11 for $29.99 for one or $99.99 for a four-pack.

Switch between two of America's best 5G networks with Google Fi

Starting today on eligible Pixels, Google Fi’s new super network delivers the nation's fastest, most expansive data coverage by automatically switching between two of America's top 5G cellular networks and millions of secure Wi-Fi networks. 9 10 11 12 Already have a Pixel but not using Google Fi? Get 50% off on select unlimited plans for 12 months. Ends 12/1/26. All terms apply. Visit the blog post, Google Fi website for details, and join Google Fi today.

Unlock your Pixel Watch with your phone

Your Pixel devices work better together. When your watch is on your wrist and you’ve unlocked your nearby phone, your Pixel Watch will automatically unlock so you can skip typing your PIN or pattern on the watch. Coming in the next few weeks. 13

Step-by-step workouts are rolling out to Pixel Watch

We’re now rolling out step-by-step workouts to Pixel Watch 3 and newer models. Whether you’re following an exercise routine created by your Google Health Coach 14 or a custom workout built in the Google Health app, you can get step-by-step instructions, log reps and weights, and track metrics directly from your Pixel Watch or your phone.

Check out our community forum post for the full list of new features arriving on your Pixel devices this month.
